task: Define validated reusable presentation tokens for existing shared commerce capabilities so engines remain template-independent, inherit Template DNA by default, and support safe local color overrides without changing runtime business authority.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The contract will be shared by multiple commerce capabilities and future templates. Strong behavioral proof is justified for inheritance, validation and authority boundaries. Formal verification is disproportionate because this slice does not alter engine state machines, transactions, persistence or checkout behavior.

deferredTechniques.reason: The style contract is bounded data validation rather than a stateful protocol.
No concurrent or transactional business authority changes.

acceptanceCriteria: Shared engines expose one reusable validated color-token contract rather than template-local styling APIs.
Omitted engine color tokens mean inherit from the active Template DNA/global storefront tokens.
Explicit local color overrides are bounded to an allowlist and valid six-digit hex colors.
Engine structure, product bindings, eligibility, pricing, stock, cart and checkout authorities are unchanged by presentation overrides.
Interactive Scene / Shop the Look uses the same styling contract as Finder, Composer, Configurator and other shared engines.
Existing engine component manifests opt into the shared engineStyle config key without introducing a second renderer or persistence model.
Unknown style keys and malformed color values fail closed.
The contract remains product/template agnostic and therefore works in future Blank Studio and VX Site-compatible capability surfaces where the engine itself is allowed.
invariants: Template DNA is the default source of colors; engine overrides are optional and local.
Engine color editing never grants capability/entitlement or parent-child insertion permission.
No raw CSS, arbitrary custom property name, HTML or JavaScript enters the engineStyle contract.
Engine business/configuration state and engine presentation state remain separate.
One engine implementation can be styled differently by different templates without forking the engine.
Style token parsing is deterministic, bounded and side-effect free.

alternatives.summary: Allow arbitrary CSS/style objects per engine.
alternatives.reason: Violates Guarded Freedom, increases performance/security risk and makes engine rendering unstable.

alternatives.summary: Use one validated semantic Engine Style Token contract inherited from Template DNA with optional local overrides.
alternatives.reason: Preserves universal engines, allows branding flexibility and keeps runtime optimization predictable.

alternatives.summary: Bake colors into each template-specific engine preset.
alternatives.reason: Recreates template-owned engines and prevents Blank Studio from composing capabilities independently.

specialistReviews.finding: Presentation must not become a second engine authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: One pure style contract is consumed by existing component configs; runtime/business APIs remain unchanged.

specialistReviews.finding: Free-form CSS/custom properties would create injection and unbounded styling surface.
specialistReviews.resolution: Allowlisted semantic token keys plus strict #RRGGBB validation only.

specialistReviews.finding: Local overrides could accidentally become mandatory and break old templates.
specialistReviews.resolution: Empty/absent engineStyle resolves to no local variables, preserving current inherited behavior exactly.

specialistReviews.finding: Merchants need brand control without understanding CSS.
specialistReviews.resolution: Expose semantic colors such as háttér/felület/szöveg/kiemelés later through Inspector; this slice creates the safe canonical data contract first.

challenge.scenario: A template inserts Shop the Look with no engineStyle config.
challenge.finding: A new contract must not change existing output.
challenge.resolution: Empty style state emits no override; inherited Template DNA remains authoritative.

challenge.finding: Partial overrides could erase inherited colors.
challenge.resolution: Only explicitly supplied token variables are emitted; all others continue inheritance.

challenge.scenario: A malicious config adds '--position' or arbitrary CSS.
challenge.resolution: Parser rejects every unknown semantic key and never accepts arbitrary CSS variable names.

challenge.scenario: Malformed colors such as url(), rgb(), 3-digit hex or CSS expressions are supplied.
challenge.resolution: Only #RRGGBB values are accepted and normalized to lowercase.

challenge.scenario: A template defines a special Shop-the-Look-only color API.
challenge.resolution: Interactive Scene uses the same generic engineStyle contract; templates provide defaults through DNA/presets only.

challenge.scenario: Engine styling changes capability or commerce binding data.
challenge.resolution: Style parser has no access to bindings/capability/runtime engine documents and returns presentation tokens only.

challenge.scenario: Many engines on one page have different local overrides.
challenge.resolution: Runtime application in the next isolated slice is scoped to each engine root; this foundation contract contains no global mutation.

challenge.scenario: Future engines need the same color editability.
challenge.resolution: Export reusable ENGINE_STYLE_CONFIG_KEY and parser/types for manifest adoption.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code against the exact stacked branch before product-code execution.
Unit-test empty inheritance, partial overrides, normalization, unknown keys, malformed values and size bounds.
Assert all targeted shared engine manifests expose exactly the same engineStyle config key.
Assert Interactive Scene remains the canonical shared Shop-the-Look/Room component and no template-local engine is introduced.
Run incremental known-failure replay for Builder/shared-storefront scope.
Run typecheck and production build on exact implementation HEAD.
Do not merge parent or child PR, update goldens or weaken release-risk gates.

requirements.requirement: Provide one validated reusable Engine Style Token contract for shared capabilities.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No raw CSS/custom-property injection or template-specific engine style authority.

requirements.requirement: Preserve Template DNA inheritance when no or partial local engine override is supplied.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The new contract must not make local styling mandatory for existing templates.

requirements.requirement: Make the shared engine families, including Interactive Scene / Shop the Look, opt into the same engineStyle config contract.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No Shop-the-Look-specific template engine or divergent styling schema is added.

requirements.requirement: Keep all business capability, binding, pricing, stock, cart and checkout authority unchanged.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Presentation tokens cannot alter entitlement, bindings or commerce truth.

notes: This is slice 1 of the PO-approved universal-engine + Blank Studio direction. It intentionally excludes runtime UI application and the Blank Studio package so the release-risk budget stays within two affected subsystems. A following stacked slice will apply local CSS-variable overrides at engine roots; Blank Studio is a separate system-template slice outside the curated 42 count. Actual-diff Plan Before Code reconciliation confirms the shared storefront-* engine definitions are dual-owned by DOMAIN-BUILDER and DOMAIN-STOREFRONT, with builder-template-system + shared-storefront authorities. Guard digest is reconciled to the exact machine projection; scope is unchanged at two subsystems.
